newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM PRECIOUS METALS END LOWER, PALLADIUM UP.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM PRECIOUS METALS END LOWER, PALLADIUM UP.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures except for palladium futures ended lower on Monday, as the dollar's slide against the yen put downward pressure on the market, traders said.

Although spot gold prices benefited from the sharp decline in the U.S. dollar, treasury bonds and stocks, uncertainty over the near-term trend in the currency market spurred profit-taking in most yen-based futures, the traders said.
Gold futures ranged from 11 yen to 16 yen per gram lower. Benchmark June was off 16 yen at 1,197 yen.
Spot gold was quoted weaker at $326.40/326.90 per ounce at 0729 GMT, against $326.90/327.40 in New York on Friday.

"Activity in gold futures was moving in line with the currency market. The participation of private investors was limited due to the Obon holidays this week and the nervous currency market," one trading house trader said.
Palladium futures ended higher on short-covering, but prices came off early highs on profit-taking, they said.
"The market was driven by technical factors. But considering unstable Russian supplies, the downside potential is limited," one trader said.
Palladium futures ranged from two yen to 33 yen per gram higher. Benchmark June was up two yen at 709 yen.
In the platinum futures market, profit-taking after the metal's recent strong performance dominated the market.

"A view that platinum prices have hit a ceiling for the near-term has appeared in the market," one commodity broker said. "A moderate downside correction is likely as the physical platinum market has not been tight as the palladium market," he said. Most-active benchmark June platinum ended down 23 yen at 1,519 yen. Benchmark June silver was off 2.7 yen per 10 grams at 166.3 yen.
